text:
amelia: Heads up — prod-usw2 model-serving started returning 502/504s ~08:11. Only for a subset of requests that go to the embeddings endpoint. Not global, looks AZ-specific.

samir: saw that too, alerts from /svc/embeddings high error rate. Rolling back a canary fixed some but errors returned after a few minutes.

chris: ran a quick dig from a pod in subnet-a (usw2-a):
```
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> embeddings.api.redwood.internal
;; ANSWER SECTION:
embeddings.api.redwood.internal. 60 IN A 18.64.122.7
```
That IP is public (AWS ELB). Should resolve to interface endpoint private IP when PrivateDNS enabled.

kai: hmm, our interface endpoint for the embeddings service had its Private DNS toggled off by the last terraform PR (drift). I saw the PR yesterday but thought the change was only tagging.

samir: if Private DNS is off then Route53 will still return public record for the service name -> split-horizon. But why intermittent? some pods resolve to private ENI and others to public?

amelia: intermittent because DNS caching + some nodes still had old resolver cache entries. Also different subnets have different resolver behavior due to a custom DNS forwarder we run for egress.

chris: verified the VPC endpoint state:
```
$ aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --vpc-endpoint-ids vpce-0a1b2c3d
{
  "VpcEndpoints": [
    {
      "VpcEndpointId": "vpce-0a1b2c3d",
      "VpcEndpointType": "Interface",
      "PrivateDnsEnabled": false,
      "NetworkInterfaces": [
        {"NetworkInterfaceId": "eni-aaa111","AvailabilityZone": "us-west-2a","PrivateIpAddress": "10.0.5.12"},
        {"NetworkInterfaceId": "eni-bbb222","AvailabilityZone": "us-west-2b","PrivateIpAddress": "10.0.9.34"}
      ],
      "DnsEntries": []
    }
  ]
}
```
PrivateDnsEnabled=false and no DNS entries -> explains dig.

kai: also noticed the endpoint SG only allowed outbound 443 and inbound from our control plane SG, not from the worker subnet SGs. That would break TCP return path if the ENI SG doesn't allow established connections or there's asymmetric SG references.

samir: interface endpoints accept traffic to the ENIs — need inbound on the endpoint SG from worker subnets on the relevant ports. Our worker SG expects return traffic only, but the endpoint SG didn't include the worker SG as allowed source.

amelia: so two issues: terraform drift turned off Private DNS and SG rules were too restrictive. Any idea which change removed PrivateDNS? recent PR #4092 touched the vpce module.

chris: PR #4092 changed the module defaults and missed overriding private_dns_enabled in the environment config. The diff:
```
- private_dns_enabled = true
+ # defaulted in module
```
CI merged it and we didn't catch the behavioral change.

infra-bot: deploy 1796304000: terraform apply completed for infra/vpce (who: chris).

kai: mitigation: re-enable Private DNS on the endpoint and add a managed rule allowing worker-sg -> endpoint-sg inbound 443. Rolling now to one AZ at a time.

samir: if we flip PrivateDNS we need to flush node DNS caches / restart kube-dns on affected nodes. Otherwise they'll keep resolving public IPs and go out via NAT (and hit public ELB), causing the error pattern.

amelia: agreed. Plan: 1) enable PrivateDNS on vpce 2) update endpoint SG to allow worker-sg inbound 443 3) rollout nodes in AZ-A first and restart coredns on those nodes 4) monitor errors for 30m 5) if stable, repeat AZ-B. I'm creating a short runbook in the incident ticket.

chris: applying sg change and flipping private dns now.

deploy-bot: infra change started: vpce-0a1b2c3d update (who: chris)

chris: done. PrivateDnsEnabled=true, SG updated to add rule source=sg-0worker:443.

kai: restarted coredns on pods in us-west-2a.

samir: errors dropped to baseline within ~2 minutes for the AZ we fixed. Can confirm embeds now resolve to ENI private IP:
```
$ kubectl exec -it test-pod -- dig +short embeddings.api.redwood.internal
10.0.5.12
```
Good.

amelia: leaving a follow-up: retro + three actions: (1) add a terraform policy test to ensure private_dns_enabled explicit, (2) add a pre-merge check to prevent removing endpoint DNS toggles, (3) add a heartbeat monitor that verifies endpoint SG pairings and DNS map. Filing ENGINFRA-1289.

chris: yep putting PR out for policy and adding a small smoke check that does dig against all env endpoints.

amelia: thanks all — incident resolved for now. Will keep monitoring for 2h and then close the thread. :white_check_mark:
